clinicalPearls: Thrombophlebitis of the superficial dorsal vein of the penis, a benign self-limiting condition
Presents as a palpable, cord-like, sometimes tender indurated structure along the dorsum of the penis
It often follows vigorous or prolonged sexual activity, and other precipitants include trauma and pelvic procedures
It is the penile analogue of Mondor disease of the chest/breast wall
Diagnosis is usually clinical, supported by Doppler ultrasound showing a thrombosed non-compressible dorsal vein
It resolves spontaneously over weeks with conservative measures such as anti-inflammatory treatment and abstinence
reference.pathophysiology: Penile Mondor disease is a localised thrombophlebitis of the superficial dorsal vein of the penis. Endothelial injury and venous stasis, often from prolonged sexual activity, trauma or compression, promote thrombosis of the superficial vein, producing a palpable thrombosed cord with surrounding inflammation. It is a benign, self-limiting vascular condition confined to the superficial penile venous system, and recanalisation occurs over time.
additionalDifferentials: Dorsal nerve or other penile pathology
additionalInvestigations: Clinical diagnosis from the palpable thrombosed dorsal cord
Doppler ultrasound of the dorsal penile vein
History of precipitating activity or trauma
Assessment for a hypercoagulable state if recurrent
Exclusion of Peyronie disease and infection
redFlags: Persistent symptoms beyond the expected course
reference.prognosis: The condition is benign and resolves spontaneously over a few weeks with conservative management, with a good prognosis and low recurrence.
pitfalls: Confusing it with Peyronie disease or sclerosing lymphangitis
Investigating or treating it as an infection
Overlooking a hypercoagulable tendency in recurrent cases
Causing undue alarm about a benign self-limiting condition
